title: Decoding an unpadded two-tape machine code
statement: Let a representation scheme encode machines with two work tapes, binary alphabet, and a finite nonempty state space of the specified form as bit strings, and decode every bit string to such a machine. Suppose that, for every such machine and every natural number of padding bits, decoding its code followed by that many $1$ bits returns the machine. Then decoding the unpadded code of each such machine returns that machine.
hypotheses_covered: A representation scheme with encoding and total decoding maps
Machines with two work tapes, binary alphabet, and state space $\{0,\ldots,m\}$ for some $m\in\mathbb{N}$
The padding law for every machine and every natural padding length
